lessons.title: Lesson 1: MVC Architecture
lessons.html:
Model-View-Controller Pattern

MVC separates concerns: Model (data), View (UI), Controller (logic). Makes code maintainable.

Structure:

  • Model: Database operations, business logic
  • View: HTML templates
  • Controller: Handles requests, coordinates Model+View
class UserController {
    public function index() {
        $model = new UserModel();
        $users = $model->getAll();
        require 'views/users/index.php';
    }
}

Benefits: Reusable components, easier testing, team collaboration.

Practice Exercises:

  1. Modify the code example to handle edge cases
  2. Write a test case for the main functionality
  3. Refactor the code to improve performance or readability

Key Takeaways:

  • Understanding the fundamental concepts is crucial for advanced topics
  • Always consider edge cases and error handling in production code
  • Practice with real-world examples to solidify your knowledge

lessons.title: Lesson 3: PDO Advanced
lessons.html:
Secure Database Operations

PDO with prepared statements prevents SQL injection. Always use!

CRUD Examples:

// CREATE
$stmt = $pdo->prepare('INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (?, ?)');
$stmt->execute(['John', 'john@example.com']);
$userId = $pdo->lastInsertId();

// READ
$stmt = $pdo->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?');
$stmt->execute([$userId]);
$user = $stmt->fetch(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);

Transactions:

$pdo->beginTransaction();
try {
    $pdo->exec('UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = 1');
    $pdo->exec('UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 100 WHERE id = 2');
    $pdo->commit();
} catch (Exception $e) {
    $pdo->rollBack();
}

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Sessions & Authentication
lessons.html:
User Sessions & Login System

Sessions track logged-in users across requests.

<?php
session_start();

// Login
if ($_POST && authenticate($_POST['email'], $_POST['password'])) {
    $_SESSION['user_id'] = $user['id'];
    $_SESSION['user_name'] = $user['name'];
    header('Location: dashboard.php');
}

Protected Pages:

<?php
session_start();
if (!isset($_SESSION['user_id'])) {
    header('Location: login.php');
    exit;
}

Security: Use password_hash(), password_verify(), HTTPS.

Building JSON APIs

APIs return JSON data for frontend apps, mobile, etc.

header('Content-Type: application/json');

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Testing with PHPUnit
lessons.html:
Comprehensive Testing in PHP

PHPUnit is the standard testing framework for PHP. Supports unit tests, integration tests, and TDD.

Test Case:

<?php
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

class UserTest extends TestCase {
    private UserRepository $repo;

    protected function setUp(): void {
        $this->repo = new UserRepository(new MemoryDatabase());
    }

    public function testCreateUser(): void {
        $user = $this->repo->create([
            'name' => 'Alice',
            'email' => 'alice@example.com'
        ]);
        $this->assertNotNull($user->getId());
        $this->assertEquals('Alice', $user->getName());
    }

    public function testEmailValidation(): void {
        $this->expectException(\InvalidArgumentException::class);
        $this->repo->create(['name' => 'Bob', 'email' => 'invalid']);
    }

    /** @dataProvider userProvider */
    public function testValidation(string $name, string $email, bool $expected): void {
        $this->assertEquals($expected, (new UserValidator())->isValid($name, $email));
    }

    public function userProvider(): array {
        return [
            ['Alice', 'alice@ex.com', true],
            ['', 'alice@ex.com', false],
            ['Alice', 'invalid', false],
        ];
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Write integration tests for the database layer
  2. Create a test suite with fixtures and groups
  3. Implement mock objects for external services

Key Takeaways:

  • setUp() runs before each test method
  • Data providers supply multiple test inputs
  • Mocks isolate unit tests from dependencies

lessons.title: Lesson 9: Queues & Job Processing
lessons.html:
Background Job Processing in Laravel

Job queues handle time-consuming tasks asynchronously, improving response times.

Job Class:

<?php
namespace App\Jobs;

use App\Models\User;
use App\Notifications\WelcomeEmail;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\ShouldQueue;
use Illuminate\Queue\InteractsWithQueue;
use Illuminate\Bus\Queueable;

class SendWelcomeEmail implements ShouldQueue
{
    use Dispatchable, InteractsWithQueue, Queueable;

    public $timeout = 120;
    public $tries = 3;
    public $backoff = [10, 30, 60];

    public function __construct(private User $user) {}

    public function handle(): void
    {
        try {
            $this->user->notify(new WelcomeEmail($this->user));
        } catch (\Exception $e) {
            $this->release(30);
        }
    }

    public function failed(\Throwable $e): void
    {
        Log::error('Job failed: ' . $e->getMessage());
    }
}

Dispatching:

SendWelcomeEmail::dispatch($user);
ProcessOrder::dispatch($order)->delay(now()->addMinutes(15));
GenerateReport::dispatch($report)->onQueue('reports');

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create a report generation job with batch processing
  2. Implement job middleware for rate limiting
  3. Monitor queue worker with Horizon

Key Takeaways:

  • Jobs run outside the HTTP request lifecycle
  • Retries handle transient failures automatically
  • Queues can be prioritized by importance

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Caching with Redis
lessons.html:
Performance Optimization with Redis

Redis provides in-memory storage for caching, sessions, and real-time features.

Cache Usage:

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Cache;

// Store
Cache::put('user_'.$id, $user, 3600);
Cache::put('settings', $settings, now()->addDays(7));

// Retrieve
$user = Cache::get('user_'.$id);

// Remember (cache + auto-update)
$users = Cache::remember('active_users', 300, function () {
    return User::where('active', true)->get();
});

// Tags for group invalidation
Cache::tags(['users'])->put('user_'.$id, $user, 3600);
Cache::tags('users')->flush();

Redis Advanced:

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Redis;

// Rate limiting
$attempts = Redis::incr('rate_limit:'.$ip);
if ($attempts === 1) Redis::expire('rate_limit:'.$ip, 60);

// Leaderboard (sorted sets)
Redis::zadd('scores', $score, $userId);
$top10 = Redis::zrevrange('scores', 0, 9, 'WITHSCORES');

// Pub/Sub
Redis::publish('notifications', json_encode(['message' => 'New update']));

Practice Exercises:

  1. Implement a full-page cache middleware
  2. Build a real-time leaderboard with sorted sets
  3. Use Redis for session storage across multiple servers

Key Takeaways:

  • Redis reduces database load significantly
  • Cache tags enable group invalidation
  • Sorted sets are perfect for leaderboards

lessons.title: Lesson 11: Event Broadcasting & WebSockets
lessons.html:
Real-Time Events with Laravel Echo

WebSockets enable real-time features like notifications and live updates.

Event Broadcasting:

class OrderStatusUpdated implements ShouldBroadcast
{
    use Dispatchable, InteractsWithSockets;

    public function __construct(public Order $order) {}

    public function broadcastOn(): array
    {
        return [
            new Channel('orders.'.$this->order->user_id),
            new PrivateChannel('admin.notifications'),
        ];
    }

    public function broadcastWith(): array
    {
        return ['order_id' => $this->order->id, 'status' => $this->order->status];
    }
}

Client-Side:

import Echo from 'laravel-echo';
import Pusher from 'pusher-js';

window.Echo = new Echo({ broadcaster: 'pusher', key: '...', cluster: '...' });

Echo.channel('orders.' + userId)
    .listen('.order.status.updated', (e) => updateOrderStatus(e.order_id, e.status));

Echo.join('chat.' + roomId)
    .here((users) => console.log('Online:', users))
    .joining((user) => console.log('Joined:', user))
    .leaving((user) => console.log('Left:', user));

  2. Implement presence channels for online status
  3. Add WebSocket notifications for background jobs

Key Takeaways:

  • Broadcasting pushes events to connected clients
  • Presence channels track user online status
  • Private channels require authorization

lessons.title: Lesson 12: API Resources & Transformation
lessons.html:
Controlling API Response Format

API resources transform models into JSON, controlling which data is exposed.

UserResource:

class UserResource extends JsonResource
{
    public function toArray(Request $request): array
    {
        return [
            'id' => $this->id,
            'name' => $this->name,
            'email' => $this->email,
            'avatar' => $this->avatar_url,
            'joined_at' => $this->created_at->toISOString(),
            'stats' => [
                'posts_count' => $this->posts_count,
                'followers_count' => $this->followers_count,
            ],
            $this->mergeWhen($request->user()?->isAdmin(), [
                'is_admin' => $this->is_admin,
            ]),
        ];
    }

    public function with(Request $request): array
    {
        return ['meta' => ['api_version' => '1.0', 'timestamp' => now()->toISOString()]];
    }
}

Resource Collection:

class UserCollection extends ResourceCollection
{
    public $collects = UserResource::class;

    public function toArray(Request $request): array
    {
        return [
            'data' => $this->collection,
            'pagination' => [
                'total' => $this->total(),
                'per_page' => $this->perPage(),
                'current_page' => $this->currentPage(),
                'total_pages' => $this->lastPage(),
            ],
        ];
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create nested resources for related models
  2. Implement conditional attribute inclusion
  3. Build a sparse fieldsets feature

Key Takeaways:

  • Resources control response shape
  • mergeWhen conditionally includes fields
  • Collections handle pagination metadata

lessons.title: Lesson 13: Advanced Eloquent ORM
lessons.html:
Eloquent Relationships & Performance

Eloquent ORM makes database interactions intuitive. Master relationships and eager loading.

Advanced Relationships:

class Post extends Model
{
    // Has-Many-Through
    public function postComments(): HasManyThrough
    {
        return $this->through('user')->has('comments');
    }

    // Polymorphic
    public function images(): MorphMany
    {
        return $this->morphMany(Image::class, 'imageable');
    }

    // Belongs-To-Many with pivot data
    public function subscribers(): BelongsToMany
    {
        return $this->belongsToMany(User::class)->withPivot(['subscribed_at', 'notify'])->withTimestamps();
    }

    // Scopes
    public function scopePublished($query) {
        return $query->whereNotNull('published_at')->where('published_at', '<=', now());
    }
}

Performance:

// Eager loading to avoid N+1
$posts = Post::with(['user', 'comments.author', 'tags'])->published()->paginate(20);

// Lazy eager loading
$posts = Post::all();
if ($includeComments) { $posts->load('comments'); }

// Chunk for large datasets
Post::chunk(100, function ($posts) { foreach ($posts as $post) { /* ... */ } });

// Cursor pagination for infinite scroll
$posts = Post::orderBy('id')->cursorPaginate(25);

Practice Exercises:

  1. Set up a polymorphic comment system
  2. Optimize a slow page with eager loading
  3. Implement a global scope for multi-tenancy

Key Takeaways:

  • Eager loading eliminates N+1 queries
  • Polymorphic relationships handle multiple parent types
  • Cursor pagination scales better than offset pagination

lessons.title: Lesson 14: Form Requests & Validation
lessons.html:
Advanced Validation Rules

Form Requests encapsulate validation logic. Custom rules keep code clean.

Form Request:

class StoreUserRequest extends FormRequest
{
    public function authorize(): bool
    {
        return $this->user()->can('create', User::class);
    }

    public function rules(): array
    {
        return [
            'name' => ['required', 'string', 'min:2', 'max:255'],
            'email' => ['required', 'email', Rule::unique('users')->ignore($this->user), 'max:255'],
            'password' => ['required', 'string', 'min:8', 'confirmed',
                'regex:/^(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*[A-Z])(?=.*\d)/'],
            'role' => ['required', Rule::in(['user', 'admin', 'moderator'])],
            'avatar' => ['nullable', 'image', 'mimes:jpeg,png', 'max:2048'],
        ];
    }

    public function messages(): array
    {
        return [
            'name.required' => 'Please provide your full name.',
            'password.regex' => 'Password needs uppercase, lowercase, and number.',
        ];
    }
}

Custom Rule:

class CurrentPassword implements ValidationRule
{
    public function validate(string $attribute, mixed $value, Closure $fail): void
    {
        if (!Hash::check($value, auth()->user()->password)) {
            $fail('The :attribute does not match your current password.');
        }
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create a custom rule for phone number validation
  2. Implement conditional validation rules
  3. Build reusable rule classes for addresses

Key Takeaways:

  • Form Requests keep controllers clean
  • Custom rules are reusable across requests
  • Conditional rules adapt to the input

lessons.title: Lesson 15: File Storage & Media Library
lessons.html:
File Management with Laravel

Laravel's filesystem supports local, S3, and cloud storage with a unified API.

File Upload:

class MediaController extends Controller
{
    public function upload(UploadRequest $request)
    {
        $file = $request->file('file');

        $path = $file->storeAs(
            'uploads/' . date('Y/m'),
            uniqid() . '.' . $file->extension(),
            's3'
        );

        // Generate thumbnail for images
        if (str_starts_with($file->getMimeType(), 'image/')) {
            $thumbnail = Image::make($file)->fit(300, 300)->encode();
            Storage::disk('s3')->put('thumbnails/' . basename($path), $thumbnail);
        }

        $media = Media::create([
            'filename' => basename($path),
            'original_name' => $file->getClientOriginalName(),
            'path' => $path,
            'mime_type' => $file->getMimeType(),
            'size' => $file->getSize(),
            'user_id' => auth()->id(),
        ]);

        return response()->json($media, 201);
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Build a media library with image optimization
  2. Implement signed URLs for private files
  3. Create a file versioning system

Key Takeaways:

  • Filesystem abstraction works with any storage provider
  • Image manipulation happens server-side
  • Thumbnails improve loading speed
